question: What a later start's new game still does differently: the laws China gives up in the two days, the three last_war pairs, the military_access line in an order of battle, New Zealand's posts and the 1939 fronts.

addresses.name: CCountry_RevertDisallowedLaws
addresses.comment: **A country at peace drops every law its `allow` no longer permits.** VA 0x4D57D0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D59BE, read whole. One caller, CCountry::OnDiplomacyChanged (0x4E7178), and only when `at_war (+0xACC)` is clear - so after any change of diplomacy (a peace among them) and never during a war. It builds one CEventScope: **country = this country, FROM = `---`, province 0, THIS = the scope itself, random state and seed 0**. Then for each law group by index from 1: the current law (`laws +0x628[i]`); if it is a real law (slot 16) and its `allow` (the CTrigger held at CLaw +0x54, slot 6) fails in that scope, the group's law list (+0xC) is walked from its head (node +0 the law, +4 the next) and **the first law met that is real, is not the current one and whose `allow` holds** is posted as `CChangeLawCommand(law, group, payCost 0, postMessage 1, country)` on the country's channel (interface_host +0xF1C, slot 18, +0x38, slot 6). None holding leaves the law. It runs for every country, the player's included, so a player sees LAW_APPOINTED for a law he did not choose, and pays nothing for it. **Corrected 2026-11-15: the list runs in the reverse of laws.txt's order** - CLawGroup::LoadKey links each new law in front of the old head (0x5297E5-0x529810: node {law, next = old head, prev 0}, head = node, old head's prev = node), the same list SetUpCountryLawsAndTechnologyForNewGame walks from the last law (FINDINGS-starttech.md section 3) - so the law posted is **the last allowed in the file's order**, not the first. Measured on the 1939.9.1 bookmark's start save: China, made Japan's puppet on the first of the two days, holds legalistic_restrictions, volunteer_army and basic_mobilisation, the last allowed of each group at its 69.998 unity and 81.291 effective neutrality, where the file's first would be limited_restrictions and full_civilian_economy. Made before in_game is set, the command keeps neither flag (the constructor), so a revert during a new game's two days is free and silent; it waits on the queue behind the new game's Laws() posts (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 16).
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x4D57D0..0x4D59BE: mov edi,[eax+0xC] then node [edi] law, [edi+4] next, first allowed real non-current posted; disasm 0x5297E5..0x529810 for the head insertion. Shown wrong by a later reorder of the list (not searched, as FINDINGS-starttech.md section 3 says), or by a save where a reverted law is the file's first allowed rather than its last.
addresses.revises: corrects 'the first law' to the last in the file's order: the list runs backwards; adds the flags before in_game

addresses.name: CCountry::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CCountry::LoadKey(CCountry* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: Slot 4 of CPersistent for a country: one key from a save, dispatched on its token id through a tree of comparisons. The value is the CToken at parse +0x228, so a number is read straight out of parse +0x22C. The mirror of CCountry::SaveContents, and the other place a field's save key can be read off. **The keys it names**, read 2026-11-14 with scripts/switchmap.py over the whole tree of comparisons - 126 cases, the closing brace and one token the table does not name among them: `color`, `duration`, `history`, `manpower`, `capital`, `technology`, `government`, `distribution`, `army`, `navy`, `home`, `leader`, `spies`, `building_construction`, `military_construction`, `graphical_culture`, `declarewar`, `allianceaction`, `guaranteeaction`, `milaccess`, `offermilaccess`, `war_exhaustion`, `callaction`, `modifier`, `to`, `flags`, `back`, `color2`, `variables`, `ideology`, `ministers`, `air`, `research`, `theatre`, `armygroup`, `corps`, `division`, `pool`, `leadership`, `influence`, `unit_deployment`, `building_deployment`, `escorts`, `convoys`, `convoy`, `convoy_construction`, `popularity`, `unit_names`, `officers`, `auto_maintain_convoy`, `auto_supply_convoy`, `auto_resource_convoy`, `nukes`, `mobilize`, `government_in_exile`, `strategic_warfare`, `acting_capital`, `default_templates`, `saved_templates`, `auto_assign_leaders`, `usage`, `active_leaders`, `convoyed_out`, `traded_for`, `traded_away`, `ai`, `human`, `active_mission`, `last_mission_cancel`, `last_election`, `slider_locks`, `major`, `last_rebel_acceptance`, `remove_fow`, `last_mission`, `historical_friends`, `ai_hard_strategy`, `ai_event_strategy`, `alignment`, `organization`, `dissent`, `national_unity`, `neutrality`, `election`, `nap`, `diplo_influence`, `influence_leaders`, `embargo_action`, `faction_action`, `trade_action`, `spy_priority`, `spy_allocation`, `spy_mission`, `spy_date`, `send_expedition`, `licence_technology`, `debtaction_action`, `peace_action`, `prov_vp`, `offmap_vp`, `spiescaught`, `share_technology`, `shared_technologies`, `traded_for_sans_allied`, `traded_away_sans_allied`, `land_battles_fought`, `air_battles_fought`, `naval_battles_fought`, `cabinet`, `effective_neutrality`, `highest_threat`, `last_surrender`, `request_lendlease`, `lendlease_targets`, `lendlease_distributions`, `covert_ops_points`, `lendlease_effectiveness`, `lend_lease_from`, `lend_lease_from_values`, `lend_lease_from_yesterday`, `lend_lease_from_yesterday_values`, `lend_lease_income`, `lend_lease_income_yesterday`, `offer_lendlease`. A technology category's name (`nocategory` among them), a law group's, a post's and another country's tag are not cases, so they are resolved past the switch (*inferred*: the default arm was not followed). Every country key in the maintainer's saves is a case, `human`, `prov_vp`, `offmap_vp`, `last_mission_cancel`, `trade_action`, `influence` and the three `*_yesterday` lend-lease keys among them, so the original reads all of them back. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-savegame.md, B.4. **Its last resort** (0x4CF237, read 2026-11-15): a key no case names is taken as text and looked up as a **country tag** (CCountryDataBase::GetTag, 0x4CF2C3); found, the country's record towards that country (diplomacy +0xE28[id]) loads the block through its slot 3 - so CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey takes it key by key, leaving what it does not name. That is how a save's pair blocks are read, and also how an **order of battle** reads `SWE = { military_access = yes }`, the first line of Their Finest Hour's GER_1941.txt, GER_DayOfInfamy.txt, GER_TheTideHasTurned.txt and GER_1944.txt (CCountry::LoadOobFile goes through this loader): Germany's record towards Sweden gets military_access, as both 1941 bookmarks' start saves hold. Not a tag: a **technology** name (the technology database's hash at +0x2C), its level read as a fixed-point number and held to a define (GetDefines +0xCC, +0x44), stored into +0x698[tech index]; then the **law database** (+0xC hash) - not followed further.
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x4CF237..0x4CF344: GetTag on the key's text, `mov edx,[ebx+0xE28]; mov ecx,[edx+eax*4]; call [vft+0xC]` with the parse context; else StringHashFind on the technology database +0x2C, else GetLawDataBase. Measured: GER->SWE military_access=yes in Ireland1941_06_22_00 and Ireland1941_12_11_00, absent at 1939.9.1, no diplomacy history for it. Shown wrong by a pair block in a save not reaching CDiplomacyStatus::LoadKey through this path.
addresses.revises: adds its last resort: a country tag loads the pair status, then a technology, then a law

addresses.name: CCountry::OnDiplomacyChanged
addresses.comment:
0x4E70A0 to the `ret 4` at 0x4E718D, 0xEE bytes, read end to end; **it abuts the function above it with no padding at all** (the bytes before the entry are `mov fs:[0],ecx; pop ebx; mov esp,ebp; pop ebp; ret`), so it is an entry only because twenty call sites say so - trap 2.

After the `CCurrentGameState` lazy-singleton boilerplate it does four things: `0x430050(state + 0xB5C, country)`; `0x5D6230(&country->units (+0xBAC))`, which walks the units checking each one's `+0x124` tag against the country database and the literal `REB`; `CConvoy::ClearPath` (rva 0xC6930) on every node of `convoys (+0xA0)`; `theatres_dirty (+0x580) = 1`; and, when `at_war (+0xACC)` is clear, `0x4D57D0(country)`.

**It writes no `CDiplomacyStatus` field and never touches `+0xE28`**, nor does any of the five functions it calls in its own body - which is the other half of wave 14's hole in 'a faction join creates no alliance'. The name is inference from the call sites: all twenty are diplomacy state changes (two in `CDeclareWarAction::Apply`, three in `CCallAllyAction::Apply`, one in `CPeaceAction::Apply`, one in `CFaction::AddCountry` at 0x4F63F5, four in `CCountry`'s own diplomacy block at 0x4E9CE5-0x4E9DB2, two in the vassal transfer at 0xD94A0, six in the event-effect module and one at 0x418DF8 in the setup code beside ApplyCustomGameSettingFaction), and clearing every convoy's path is what a change in who you may pass through implies. **The twenty sites by function** (2026-11-15, findRefs --callers and the record's entries): CustomGame_LeaveFaction 0x418DF8; MakeVassal 0x4DA410 and 0x4DA41E (the overlord, then the vassal, its step 13); **CCountry_Capitulate** 0x4E9CE5, 0x4E9D75, 0x4E9DA0, 0x4E9DB2 (the 'diplomacy block' above); CFaction::AddCountry 0x4F63F5; CLeaveFactionEffect::Execute 0x9A234E; CEndWarEffect::Execute 0x9B81EE, 0x9B825E, 0x9B8273; CUndeclaredWarRegionEffect::Execute 0x9BD0DB, 0x9BD0F4; CDeclareWarAction::Apply 0xA12EAC, 0xA12ECA; CCallAllyAction::Apply 0xA289E8, 0xA28A0A, 0xA28A27; CPeaceAction::Apply 0xA40169. **None is in CWar::RemoveAttacker, CWar::RemoveDefender, RemoveLandlessCountriesFromWars or AnnexCountry**: leaving a side tells nobody of a change of diplomacy unless the caller does, so the end of a new game's entry reverts no law (the Baltic states keep their war laws at both 1941 bookmarks, measured) and a puppet's enemies are not told.
addresses.evidence: findRefs.py --callers 0x4E70A0: 20 direct calls; each site placed in the nearest recorded function at or below it (MakeVassal 0x4D94A0..0x4DA447, CCountry_Capitulate 0x4E9220..0x4EA085 by their recorded extents). The function is not virtual, so the direct calls are all. Shown wrong by an indirect call (a thunk or a table) reaching it.
addresses.revises: places each of the twenty call sites in its function, and says which routines make no change of diplomacy

addresses.name: RemoveLandlessCountriesFromWars
addresses.comment: For every country of the state's array (+0xBBC) that owns no province (OwnedProvinces.count <= 0) and is not a government in exile (+0x95): CWar::RemoveAttacker / RemoveDefender (recordHistory 0) from every active war (+0xC00) it is on, then, if its faction is real, CFaction::RemoveMember, faction = CFaction::null(), RebuildStaticModifiers, RebuildRules and its display dirty byte. One caller, VA 0x65CE7D inside CInGameIdler::Enter - so it runs as a session comes up, not hourly. `ret 4`. **It tells nobody of a change of diplomacy** (2026-11-15): no call of CCountry::OnDiplomacyChanged here or in the war's own removal, so neither the landless country nor its enemies are reverted out of laws a war allowed - measured, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania keep repression, service_by_requirement and total_economic_mobilisation in both 1941 bookmarks' start saves. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 16.
addresses.evidence: The twenty callers of 0x4E70A0 (findRefs) lie outside 0x689EA0's body and outside CWar::RemoveAttacker 0xA50440..0xA506A8 and RemoveDefender 0xA51710..0xA51C37. Shown wrong by a save where a landless country at war in the history holds a peace-time law.
addresses.revises: adds that it tells nobody of a change of diplomacy, measured on the 1941 saves

addresses.name: SetUpCountryForNewGame
addresses.comment:
**What a country starts a new game with**: the effects of the decisions its history says it has taken, its war exhaustion, its stockpile, its diplomatic influence, **its relation with every other country and its first spy allocation**, its manpower, **and its pool of ministers and any empty cabinet post**. One stack argument, `ret 4` at 0x4D757A. One caller, 0x65B4F2 in CInGameIdler::Enter, inside the block that gamestate->loaded_from_save (+0xD9C) == 0 guards, so it never runs on a load. **The function before it ends `ret 4` at 0x4D622D with no padding** - a walk back from inside this one answers 0x4D59D0, which is what fieldchain.py prints (trap 2). (Addresses in this comment are VAs.)

**The decisions** (VA 0x4D6342-0x4D668A, read 2026-10-12): after UpdateIC(country, 0) at 0x4D633D it builds a CEventScope whose country is this one (CCountry +0xCA4), FROM `---`, province 0, and **random_state, its copy and seed all 0**, and walks the country's **taken list** (+0x128, next at node +0x20) - the names its history's `decision = <name>` entries put there, less any `remove_decision`, through CCountryDecisionChange::Apply. Each name is looked up **in the political table first and then the diplomatic** (the reverse of CExecuteDecisionCommand's order); not found, it logs `<TAG> has unknown decision '<name>'` under country.cpp; found, **its effect runs** - CEffect::Execute (slot 11) with (scope, 0) at 0x4D6658. Neither `potential` nor `allow` is asked, no message is raised and no history entry is filed. The scope's random state is never reset between decisions, so each draws on where the one before left it.

**The pool of ministers** (VA 0x4D6741-0x4D683C, read 2026-10-14, FINDINGS-government.md A.6): for each minister of HistoricalMinisters (+0x170) in file order, **appended to PossibleMinisters (+0x160) when `start_date (+0x54) <= now < death_date (+0x58)`** - no test that he is there already. (The two Date-to-text calls inside the loop, 0x44C710, build strings that are thrown away.) A minister with no `death_date` keeps g_NullDate there, which no `now` is below - **but the start save has every such minister in the pool**: see FINDINGS-government.md A.6 for that open contradiction.

Read from 0x4D69DF to 0x4D7108 and from 0x4D7346 to the end. Months are calendar months, year * 12 + month off the tick. At war (at_war, +0xACC): began = the earliest CWar::GetStartDate over the active wars (gamestate +0xC00) whose attackers (+0x2C..+0x30) or defenders (+0x3C..+0x40) hold the country's id - **the war's first dated history entry, not the day the country joined it**, so a country joining a long war at a later bookmark is counted at war from the war's start (the Soviet Union at 1941.6.22: 21 months from World War II's 1939.9.1) - and war_exhaustion (+0xAD0) = min(months since * 0.05, 10). Otherwise war_exhaustion = max(3 - months since the latest CWar_GetLastHistoryDate over the previous_war (+0xC20) entries the country is on, the same side test, * 0.05, 0), the latest starting at g_NullDate. **That finds nothing for a war of the history**: a history war ends by rem_attacker/rem_defender, whose CRemoveAttackerChange::Apply is CWar::RemoveAttacker, which erases the tag - a finished war has no sides left (the start save's previous_war blocks have no attacker or defender line) - so every country at peace starts at 0; a dead rule (FINDINGS-laterstart.md section 5). Then **days = 30 + 5 * max(12 - months at war, 2)** - 90 at peace, five fewer a month of war, never under 40 - and amount = MaxIC (+0x60C) * days, **held to 1000 for a subject (isSubject, +0xF34)**. Into the acting capital's pool, each an `add`: crude oil and metal `amount`, energy twice it, rare materials half; money, **only when the pool has none**, amount * IC_TO_MONEY * 0.05; supplies and fuel, `days` times the sum of CUnit::SupplyConsumption and CUnit::FuelConsumption over the country's units (+0xBAC). Then **diplo_influence (+0xA88) = MaxIC / 5 in whole points**. The 0.05 is g_OneTwentieth.

**The dates** (0x4D6841 loop, read 2026-10-12): for every country of the database, a pair whose war_seen_tick (`last_war`, +0x54) is later than now is put back to g_NullDate. Then (0x4D6912..0x4D69D5, read 2026-11-15) for each active war (gamestate +0xC00) the country is on: as an attacker its record towards every defender, else as a defender towards every attacker, gets last_war = now - the same stamp Enter's UpdateAtWarAndEnemies has just given. The lobby's replay of the history's wars stamps both the joiner's record and each enemy's at the defines' start_date (CWar::AddAttacker and AddDefender call UpdateAtWarAndEnemies on both), which the start saves show both ways for every pair whose countries still own land - a save writes no record towards a country owning none (FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 16).

**The relations** (0x4D710E..0x4D733F, read 2026-10-12, FINDINGS-diplostate.md): skipped whole for REB and for a country that owns no province (+0xCF8). Otherwise for every country B of the database in order, REB and itself included: value = 25; when B is not REB and owns a province, value = the Lua global **`AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation(country, B)`** (script/ai_country.lua; the call is built by PrepareLuaCall_AI_GenerateNonHistoricalRelation, 0x5100D0, and run by 0x50D2F0 for an integer - see the Lua paragraph below), whole points. Then, **only when `diplomacy[B]->relation (+0x38)` is exactly 0**, it becomes clamp(value * 1000, -200000, 200000) with `changed (+0x59) = 1` - **this country's side only**. So a relation the history set is kept, a computed 0 is written as 0, and an existing country is left with 25 towards REB and towards every country that does not exist. In the same loop, for a B that exists and is not REB, the first spy allocation - entry +0 of the 0xF8-byte record B in the array at espionage (+0x1160) - is 1000 * score clamped to [0, g_MaxSpyLevel], score = [value < -100] + [value < 0] + neighbours[B] (+0xF58) + [same continent (+0x368 of each acting capital)] + 2 * [both factions valid and different] + [ruling_ideology (+0x1140) differs] + 2 * [diplomacy[B]->war] - 2 * [diplomacy[B]->alliance] + 3 * [B is this country], **halved toward zero when CCountry::IsMajor (0x4F8AB0) says no**. Against the start save the non-self entries of Germany's row agree; the self entries are 1 higher for the seven majors (5, not 4) and for China (3, not 2) - **that spy is CDistributeEspionage::Distribute's, on one of the two days a new game runs before the save**: those eight are exactly the countries whose daily espionage gain reaches half a spy, and the home presence at priority 1 is the only one in a band above 0 (reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md section A). The other 70 that hold land are at 2, and the 23 that hold none at 0.

**The tail is the manpower and the cabinet.** ReapplyAllTechnologies (0x4D7346), **the Lua global `Laws(country)`** (0x4D734B-0x4D7375, below), RebuildStaticModifiers (0x4D7380), UpdateMaxManpower (0x4D7386), and then **manpower (+0xBCC) = max_manpower (+0xBD0)**, a `mov` - so whatever `manpower` a country's history file gave is overwritten. If it owns a province (the count at +0xCF8 above 0) and is at war, it then loses year * (1000 + months at war * g_StartingManpowerLostPerMonthAtWar / 1000) / 1000, where year = max_manpower * 1000 / MAX_MANPOWER and the months are the same thousandths the war exhaustion used; floored at 0. Then **last_election (+0xAB0) = now where it holds a date before year 3** (0x4D7476-0x4D752F), **CCountry_FillMinisterPosts(country, 0, 0)** (0x4D7538 - empty posts only, from the pool above), CCountry_AllotCabinetSeats (0x4D753E), and **where `ruling_ideology (+0x1140)` is null or its slot 17 says no, the ruling ideology becomes the head of state's** (`ministers[1]->ideology (+0x6C)`, 0x4D7543-0x4D7564). The CChangeLawCommands `Laws(country)` posts are made before `in_game` is set, so their pay_cost and post_message are cleared: free and silent.

**The head** (VA 0x4D6230-0x4D633B, read 2026-11-15; FINDINGS-government.md section A had it): where last_election (+0xAB0) is not g_NullDate and is before the tick, the term is the country's own duration (+0x98), else its government's (CGovernment +0x2C); n = how many terms AddMonths adds one at a time until the date is past now, and then last_election += (n - 1) terms in one AddMonths - **the latest election date of its schedule on or before the start**. With a term of 0 the counting loop never ends (inferred; whether any history gives a last_election under a government with no duration was not searched). Then UpdateIC(country, 0) at 0x4D633D. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-laterstart.md, section 4.

**The two Lua calls** (read 2026-10-12, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-luahost.md; VAs). Both take the main thread's state from GetThreadLuaState and sit in try blocks whose only handler is `catch (luabind::error&)` (FuncInfo 0x16C98D8: states 22-23 handler 0x4D7324, state 25 handler 0x4D73CF), and each handler only calls ReportLuaError (0xAA8050, `LUA Error:` in the log) and resumes after the call. **The relation**: [ebp-0x20] is set to 25 at 0x4D7173 before the call and is the result only if the call returns, so **a missing function or a Lua error leaves 25**; the result is `lua_tointeger` of a value that must be a number - `fld`/`fistp` in the Lua DLL, so **rounded to nearest, ties to even**, not truncated - and anything else (nil, a string, a boolean) throws `luabind::cast_failed`, which is **not** a `luabind::error` (its ThrowInfo 0x164B1E4 lists only cast_failed and std::exception) and so escapes this function and CInGameIdler::Enter, which has no try block at all. The country goes in as a `CCountry*` (pushed as a pointer instance, nil if null) and B as a **fresh copy of its CCountryTag**. **`Laws(country)`**: built by PrepareLuaCall_Laws (0x510120) and made by LuaCallProxy_Country_CallVoid (0x50D3F0) with one argument and no result, **for every country this function runs for, with no test of who plays it** - so `script/ai_politics_minister.lua`'s `Laws(minister)` runs with the CCountry where it expects a minister, which works because CCountry also has GetCountryTag, and posts a CChangeLawCommand for each law group it wants moved. That is how the script runs before the first hour (the open question in FINDINGS-unitstart.md).
addresses.evidence: disasm 0x4D6912..0x4D69D5: walks [state+0xC00] nodes, tests the country's id in +0x2C..+0x30 and +0x3C..+0x40, writes [ebp-0x1C] (now) into diplomacy[other]+0x54 over the other side. Measured: every last_war of the four start saves (52, 336, 503 and 2 pairs) reproduced by stamping both sides of each history join. Shown wrong by a save holding a 1936.1.1 last_war on one side only between two countries that both own land.
addresses.revises: adds the second date loop, the last_war stamp of each active war's enemies, and the replay's two-sided stamp
